newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut t-bill issue raises 291.5 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Beirut t-bill issue raises 291.5 bln pounds.

text.p: Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of May 22 raised 291.5 billion Lebanese pounds, according to finance ministry results issued on Monday.
The previous issue raised 465 billion pounds.
The issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 128 billion pounds. It raised the following amounts (in billion of pounds, previous week in brackets):

The central bank said only seven percent of all competitive bids -- those made by Lebanese institutions -- were accepted up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills, 13 percent for six-month bills, 25 percent for one-year bills and 75 percent for two-year bills.

It also restricted the acceptance of non-competitive bids -- those made by private individuals and foreign investors -- for the shorter-term bills, approving seven percent up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and 13 percent for six-month bills.
As for longer-term bills, all non-competitive bids were accepted, it said.
The Lebanese pound closed at 1,542.25 to the U.S. dollar on Monday from 1,542 a week earlier and 1,575.5 a year ago.
